html:
SMTO-EXE-0074 — SMTO couldn't use that file location for the clipboard

GUID: 7ababa23-3ad2-5085-bd0d-437a6d6c4467
Slug: clipboard-invalid-path
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • To copy files to the Gateway computer's clipboard, SMTO needs the full location of files that already exist on that computer. The location was incomplete, on a network drive, a web link, or the file wasn't there.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Give SMTO the file's full location on the Gateway computer, starting from the drive or top folder, for example C:\Users\Public\Documents\report.pdf or /home/alex/report.pdf. SMTO refuses partial locations because it can't be sure which file you mean.
  2. If the file is on your own device, a shared network drive or a website, first move or download it onto the Gateway computer. SMTO only puts files on the clipboard that are stored on the Gateway computer itself.
  3. If SMTO was reading files you copied, copy them again from a local folder on the Gateway computer, not from a network share. Files copied from network locations are refused when SMTO reads them from the clipboard.

What success looks like

  • SMTO confirms how many files it put on the clipboard, or lists the files it read.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway, with the folder the files are in. Don't put the files in a shared network folder to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Clipboard file-path validation rejected a relative, malformed, network (UNC or //), device or non-local file-URI path, a required file that does not exist on the Gateway, or an invalid native path result.

What this means

  • Clipboard file validation rejected malformed/relative/network/device paths, unsupported URI hosts/escapes, nonexistent required files or an invalid native path result. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Clipboard file validation rejected malformed/relative/network/device paths, unsupported URI hosts/escapes, nonexistent required files or an invalid native path result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact target-local path form and existence requirement, including URI decoding and Windows network/device restrictions.

How to fix it

  • Supply existing absolute local paths on the selected Gateway (a drive-letter path on Windows, a path starting with a single / on Linux and macOS); network paths, URLs, relative paths and paths with control characters are rejected. Transfer files from the Server or other machines to that Gateway first.
  • Supply an existing absolute local path on the selected Gateway; transfer controller files there first. Network paths and URLs are unsupported.

Retry and execution caution

  • Supply an existing absolute local path on the selected Gateway; transfer controller files there first. Network paths and URLs are unsupported.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended existing local paths validate on the same Gateway before clipboard mutation.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
